title: Worksheet 7: How Search Engines Work
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A search engine, such as Google or Bing, helps people find information on the internet by searching through billions of webpages in a fraction of a second. Search engines are able to respond so quickly because they do not actually search the entire internet at the exact moment you type a query. Instead, they use programs called "web crawlers" or "spiders" that constantly scan the internet ahead of time, visiting webpages and following links to other pages. Information about each webpage is then stored in a massive, organized database called an "index." When a person types a search, the search engine quickly looks through this pre-built index, rather than the live internet, to find matching results. The search engine then uses a ranking system to decide which results are most likely to be useful, considering factors such as how relevant the page is to the search words and how many other trustworthy websites link to it, before displaying the results in order.
